metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL MySQL OTel] InnoDB deadlocks and lock wait timeouts
metadata.description: Alerts when statements on a Cloud SQL for MySQL instance fail on row locks at an average of at least 1 per minute over the last 15 minutes. Failures are deadlocks (database/mysql/innodb/deadlocks_count, where a transaction was rolled back) plus lock wait timeouts (lock_timeout_count, where a statement gave up after innodb_lock_wait_timeout). Rates are per reported minute, so gaps and duplicate points don't skew them, and each count needs at least 5 reported minutes to contribute. Each failure is an application error unless the client retries.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_mysql.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// One-minute delta counts: deadlocks (transaction rolled back) and lock wait timeouts (statement failed after
// innodb_lock_wait_timeout). Both metrics are MySQL-only, so the rule is MySQL-scoped.
| STATS deadlocks = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/innodb/deadlocks_count`)),
        deadlock_samples = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/innodb/deadlocks_count`)),
        lock_timeouts = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/innodb/lock_timeout_count`)),
        lock_timeout_samples = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/mysql/innodb/lock_timeout_count`))
  BY database_id

data.content:
## Cloud SQL MySQL InnoDB deadlocks and lock wait timeouts

Statements are failing on row locks. A deadlock rolls back one transaction; a lock wait timeout fails the statement after `innodb_lock_wait_timeout` (50 seconds by default).

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] Cloud SQL MySQL Instance Detail** and check *Deadlocks over time* and *Row lock waits and lock timeouts*. Note when the failures started and whether a deployment or batch job started at the same time.
2. On the instance, run `SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS` (*LATEST DETECTED DEADLOCK* section). Query `sys.innodb_lock_waits` and `information_schema.innodb_trx` to find the blocking and long-running transactions.
3. Lock timeouts usually mean one long transaction holds locks that others wait for: an idle open transaction, a slow batch update or a stuck session.

### Actions
Kill the blocking session if it's safe to do so. Long-term fixes are in the application: keep transactions short, access rows in a consistent order, index the columns used to look up locked rows, and retry deadlocked transactions.

### Tuning
Change `lock_failures_per_min >= 1.0` to adjust the threshold. Applications that retry deadlocks by design can tolerate a higher deadlock rate.
